No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result FCT Group Condemns Attack On Tinubu’s Convoy by Igho Oyoyo 6 seconds ago in News Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Stakeholders Assembly has condemned the attack on the convoy of President Bola Tinubu at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in Abuja, describing it as an affront to the dignity of the Office of the President
and a threat to the country’s democratic values, political stability and national unity. The Assembly also reaffirmed its unwavering support for Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, declaring that the incident would not weaken its resolve to mobilise residents and indigenous communities across the FCT for the President’s second-term ambition.
The president of the Assembly, Aliyu Daniel Kwali, stated this in a statement on Saturday condemning the attack, which occurred on Friday, November 13, 2026.
Kwali described the incident as “barbaric and reprehensible,” insisting that such conduct was unacceptable in a democratic society and should not be allowed to undermine the nation’s political stability.
“We consider this unfortunate incident a direct affront to the dignity of the Office of the President and a disturbing threat to our democratic values, political stability and national unity,” he said.
The Assembly consequently called on relevant security agencies to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the incident, identify those responsible and ensure that they are brought to justice.
It expressed particular concern that the attack occurred barely 14 days after law-abiding citizens of the FCT, under the platform of the FCT Stakeholders Assembly, unanimously endorsed President Tinubu and Vice President Kashim
Shettima as their preferred candidates for the 2027 presidential election.
According to the group, the timing of the incident raises serious questions about the growing desperation and intolerance among certain political interests.
“Coming barely fourteen days after the law-abiding citizens of the Federal Capital Territory, under the auspices of the FCT Stakeholders Assembly, unanimously endorsed President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima as their preferred candidates for the 2027 Presidential Election, this unfortunate incident raises serious concerns about the growing desperation and intolerance within certain political quarters,” the statement said.
The Assembly, however, stressed that the actions of a few individuals should not be misconstrued as the position of the entire FCT, insisting that the majority of residents and original inhabitants remained committed to peace, democratic participation and the rule of law.
It described itself as a unifying platform representing the interests of original inhabitants and residents across the territory, adding that its commitment to peaceful coexistence and political tolerance remained unwavering.
The group also reiterated its confidence in the leadership of President Tinubu and its commitment to his administration and the Renewed Hope Agenda.
“We wish to make it unequivocally clear that the actions of a few misguided individuals do not represent the collective position, political aspirations or democratic convictions of the peace-loving and law-abiding people of the FCT,” it stated.
The Assembly further assured the President that the incident would not intimidate its members or discourage them from supporting his administration and political aspirations ahead of the general elections.
It declared that no act of intimidation, political provocation or mischief by any individual or group would diminish its confidence in Tinubu’s leadership or weaken its collective resolve.
“We therefore assure Mr. President that no act of intimidation, political provocation or mischief by any individual or group will diminish our confidence in his leadership or weaken our collective resolve,” the statement added.
Reaffirming its position on the 2027 presidential election, the Assembly said its endorsement of Tinubu and Shettima remained firm, while pledging to intensify mobilisation across its structures and constituents in the FCT.
“Our endorsement remains firm, our commitment remains unwavering, and our support remains resolute. We stand firmly with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and remain committed to mobilising our structures and constituents towards securing his re-election on January 16, 2027,” Kwali declared.
The Assembly also urged political actors, supporters and other stakeholders to exercise restraint and embrace peaceful, issue-based political engagement as the country approaches the 2027 general elections.
It warned against actions that could escalate political tensions, threaten public safety or undermine democratic values, emphasising that political differences should be resolved through peaceful and lawful means.
The statement concluded with renewed expressions of solidarity with the President, the Federal Capital Territory and the country.
